author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction changes that visit in place, adds no new visit, and passes the same checks as booking.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the visit's current date and description are shown ready to change
given a booked visit, when a valid new date and description are submitted, then that visit changes, the pet gains no visit, and the owner's record opens
given a blank description or a date of today or earlier, when a correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the field is named, and the visit stays unchanged
edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, is refused
edge case 4: correcting a visit that does not exist is refused rather than showing an empty correction
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still declined)
any link or button into the correction from the owner detail page (owner decision: reachable by URL alone in this request)
correcting a past visit without moving its date later than today (open question in the PRD)
notes: Owner-stated surface, quoted from the intake (line 1), for the design expert: "GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit form prefilled"; "Reuse the existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit` model attribute"; "POST to the same URL validates like visit creation"; "redirects to the owner detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form." Edge cases 3 and 4 are my narrowest-reading decisions, mirroring REQ-VIS-001 edge 1 and REQ-OWN-003 edge 2. The PRD delta also carries the narrowing ADR docs/adr/2026-10-24-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md and the status amendment on the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR. Test names follow the BDD school; merge the validation cases into one data-driven test.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the existing VisitController booking seam with one adjustment (system-design.md § Contracts, VisitController/Pet rows; § Overview aggregate rule: visits reached through Owner then Pet, written only via OwnerRepository cascade). NG-5 is narrowed by docs/adr/2026-10-24-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md, so no conflict. The adjustment: VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") loader runs before EVERY handler and today creates a new Visit and attaches it to the pet. Left unchanged, the edit handlers would bind onto that phantom visit and save would insert a second visit, breaking 'the pet gains no visit'. The loader therefore takes an optional visitId path variable: absent, it keeps today's new-visit behavior; present, it resolves the existing visit via owner.getPet(petId) then a new Pet.getVisit(Integer) (mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer), returns null when absent) and attaches nothing. GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit returns pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm; POST to the same URL applies the same @Valid + non-future-date check as booking, redisplays the form on error without saving, else owners.save(owner) and redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. The template needs no change: its form has no action, so it posts to the current URL, and visit['new'] already drops the 'New' heading for a persisted visit. Basis: grep and read of VisitController.java, Pet.java, Owner.java, the template (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis).
integration_points: Binding (new GET/POST .../visits/{visitId}/edit): target is the persisted Visit resolved through owner and pet, behind an allow-list. Replace VisitController's @InitBinder deny-list (setDisallowedFields id, *.id) with setAllowedFields("date", "description"). This also narrows the booking route's binding; booking behavior is unchanged because Visit has no other bindable form field (the template's hidden petId has no Visit property). security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries; system-design.md § Threat Model mass-assignment row (updated).

Repository boundary in VisitControllerTests: keep the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository. A hand-written double of a full JpaRepository interface is disproportionate in a @WebMvcTest that already wires this stub (testing-principles mocking policy: Mockito tolerated). Assert 'changes in place, pet gains no visit' by capturing the saved Owner and checking the pet's visit count and the visit's id, date, and description. Assert 'visit stays unchanged' on refusal with verify(owners, never()).save(any()).
Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch, binding, and validation (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Refusal path (edge cases 3 and 4): a missing or foreign visit raises IllegalArgumentException from the loader, the same refusal form as the REQ-VIS-001 edge 1 owner and pet checks. It surfaces as the error page, never as an empty form. Under MockMvc, assert the thrown ServletException whose cause is IllegalArgumentException.

risks.mitigation: system-design.md § Scale and Load row 'One pet's visits, resolved by identity': bounded, simplest readable form (linear scan).

risks.risk: Validation-failure binding mutates the loaded Visit object
risks.mitigation: open-in-view is disabled (system-design.md § Persistence), so the object is detached. Nothing persists unless save is called, and the error path never calls it.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: system-design.md assigns identity lookup of a visit to Pet ('resolves one of them by identity'), a seam below the controller boundary. Its only coverage is through the VisitControllerTests MockMvc slice. `ls src/test/java/.../owner/` lists no Pet test and `grep -rn 'getVisit(' src/test` finds no direct call. The rule has decision paths a unit test would pin: a persisted match, no match, an unsaved visit (visit.isNew()) with the same id is skipped, and a null id. A mutation of the `!visit.isNew()` guard, or of Objects.equals to a reference comparison, survives the controller tests because they use only small Integer ids.
findings.fix: Add a Pet unit test (e.g. PetTests) using the real Pet/Visit with one case per path, named the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. Keep the controller tests to one representative path.

findings.description: VisitController.setAllowedFields changed from setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") to setAllowedFields("date","description") for both booking and correction, and system-design.md records it as the mass-assignment mitigation. No test posts an `id` (or other) parameter, so removing the allowlist, or dropping the id guard, fails nothing. The correction test posts only date and description.
findings.fix: Add a test that posts the correction with an extra id=<other value> parameter and asserts the saved visit still has BOOKED_VISIT_ID (whole-object comparison as in the existing test).

findings.description: The TODAY and YESTERDAY rows exercise the same decision path (!isAfter(now)) with the same refused field. The boundary the code compares on is today vs tomorrow, and no row pins tomorrow as accepted. The YESTERDAY row catches no change that the TODAY row would not.
findings.fix: Drop the YESTERDAY row, or replace it with a case that accepts tomorrow (LocalDate.now().plusDays(1)) so the boundary is pinned from both sides.

findings.description: The outcome is read through an ArgumentCaptor and a getPet(...).getVisits() chain instead of comparing a whole expected object; the brief requires whole-object comparison where one can be built. The verify(this.owners).save(...) captor is the interaction, not the outcome, and the brief tolerates Mockito stubs rather than encouraging them.
findings.fix: Compare the saved Owner (or its pet's visits) to a whole expected Owner built with the suite's createAnOwnerWith/createAPet/createAVisit helpers, via usingRecursiveComparison.

semantic_surprise.note: The one change a reader would not expect is that the controller-wide @InitBinder switches from denying id/*.id to allowing only date and description, so the existing booking POST and its @ModelAttribute Owner now bind less; the template submits only date, description and a hidden petId the Visit never bound, so booking behaves the same and owner-field mass assignment is closed. The design-block prescribed this switch and the threat-model row records it. The loader returns the existing visit when visitId is present and attaches no new one, and Pet.getVisit compares by value and skips unsaved visits.

test_adequacy.note: The controller tests compare the whole saved Owner graph, which proves the visit changed in place and the pet gained no visit. They pin the date boundary from both sides (today refused, tomorrow accepted), cover a smuggled id, a cross-pet visit, an unknown pet and a missing visit, and verify that no save happens on refusal. PetTests uses ids outside the Integer cache, so a reference comparison or a dropped isNew guard would fail. The narrowed binding on the booking route has no dedicated test.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved in the end, but the round-2 approvals carry recommendations: test-reviewer says the missing-visit test and the cross-pet row reach the same path and the fixtures are duplicated, and code-quality wants Optional instead of null from Pet.getVisit. Round 1 also noted that the correction form keeps the 'Add Visit' button label, and the final doc-reviewer pass says it did not re-verify its round-1 aspects. The security reviewer's unconfigured dependency check is a standing project gap, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: There were no build retries and no design revisions. The one consultation, recorded as a consultation-response, was about vocabulary. It added Book and Correction to the ubiquitous language, defining Correction across Owner, Pet and Visit, which is broader than the slice, and it leaves that as an open owner question. The code adds only the two edit routes the intake named, adds no entry link, and implements no cancellation, as decided.

rationale: The code is a contained, well-tested correction route, and the controller-wide binder narrowing is deliberate and safe. The scrutinize comes from residual reviewer recommendations: the 'Add Visit' label on the correction form, Optional over null, and duplicated test fixtures. Read those, and check the PRD's two new open questions on past-visit corrections and entry points.
